en: Proverbs 27

p.src: 1  Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.

ja: をもたらすか、あなたには
en: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
u.src: 1  Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.

p.src: 2  Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.

ja: ではなく、 見知らぬ人に。
en: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
u.src: 2  Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.

p.src: 3  A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.

ja: は重荷となる。 しかし、
の挑発は、その両方よりも
en: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
u.src: 3  A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.

p.src: 4  Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?

ja: す洪水のようだ。 しかし、ねたみの
en: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?
u.src: 4  Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?

p.src: 5  Better is open rebuke than hidden love.

ja: よりも、 あからさまな叱責のほうが良い。
en: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
u.src: 5  Better is open rebuke than hidden love.

p.src: 6  The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

en: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
u.src: 6  The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

p.src: 7  A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.

en: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.
u.src: 7  A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.

p.src: 8  As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.

ja: れてさまよう人もそうである。
en: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
u.src: 8  As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.

p.src: 9  Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.

en: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
u.src: 9  Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.

p.src: 10  Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.

ja: より、近くにいる隣人のほうが良い。
en: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.
u.src: 10  Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.

p.src: 11  Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.

ja: ばせよ。 そうすれば、私をそしる
en: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
u.src: 11  Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.

p.src: 12  A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

en: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
u.src: 12  A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

p.src: 13  Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!

ja: れ。 道を踏み外した
en: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!
u.src: 13  Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!

p.src: 14  He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.

en: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.
u.src: 14  He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.

p.src: 15  A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:

en: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:
u.src: 15  A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:

p.src: 16  restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.

en: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.
u.src: 16  restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.

p.src: 17  Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

en: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
u.src: 17  Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

p.src: 18  Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.

en: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.
u.src: 18  Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.

p.src: 19  Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.

en: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
u.src: 19  Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.

p.src: 20  Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.

ja: も決して満ち足りない。
en: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
u.src: 20  Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.

ja: 27:20 よみ（シェオル）は死者の場所である。
en: 27:20 Sheol is the place of the dead.

p.src: 21  The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.

en: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
u.src: 21  The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.

p.src: 22  Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.

ja: を穀粒と共に乳鉢へ入れ、きねで突き
en: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
u.src: 22  Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.

p.src: 23  Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,

en: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,
u.src: 23  Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,

p.src: 24  for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.

ja: 々にわたって残るものではない。
en: for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
u.src: 24  for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.

p.src: 25  The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.

ja: が取り去られると、新しい
en: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
u.src: 25  The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.

p.src: 26  The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.

en: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
u.src: 26  The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.

p.src: 27  There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.

en: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
u.src: 27  There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
